page.overview:
What is Witch Weekly?

Witch Weekly was a popular magazine for witches created by Tobias Misslethorpe. It included articles, quizzes, advice columns, and recipes. It also reported a great deal of celebrity news, as Harry Potter and Quidditch players were featured often in it.

During the 1920s, the magazine was ran by the French newspaper Le Cri de la Gargouille and was based out of their Place Cachée headquarters in office 10.

During the Hogwarts anniversary celebrations in the 1984–1985 school year, the magazine ran an article on Minerva McGonagall, who was featured on the front page of that issue. They also gave her a personal copy to keep, which she then later gave to Jacob's sibling after signing it.

Molly Weasley was one subscriber; St Mungo's also kept it stocked in their waiting room. It gave a regular Most Charming Smile Award in association with the Witches' League (of which Lady Wimborne was president), which Gilderoy Lockhart had won five times by 1992.
